note: Real products picked by True EDC. Budget tiers are approximate; check the retailer for today's price. Retailer links are affiliate links (paid links).

products.name: Victorinox Classic SD
facts: 7 functions, including a small blade, screwdriver and key ring
Small enough to live on a keychain
products.summary: The gift nobody returns. It is small enough to forget about until the moment someone needs to open a package, trim a thread or tighten a screw, and then they never forget who gave it to them.

products.name: Nitecore THUMB LEO
products.summary: A tiny clip-on light with a tilting head and a UV mode for spotting stains, checking bills or finding a pet accident. It hangs off keys, a zipper or a cap brim.

products.name: Nite Ize S-Biner MicroLock (2-pack)
products.summary: The cheapest upgrade in EDC. It splits car keys from house keys and lets a light or a knife come off the ring in a second. Perfect stocking filler.

products.name: Field Notes Original Kraft (3-pack)
facts: 3.5 x 5.5 inches, fits a back pocket
products.summary: For the person who still writes things down. It fits in a back pocket and has a cult following, so it reads as a thoughtful gift, not a cheap one.

products.name: Casio F-91W
facts: Digital sport watch with a resin strap
products.summary: The most famous cheap watch in the world. It is light enough to wear to bed and cheap enough to wear to the gym, which is exactly why people end up wearing it every day.

products.name: Fisher Space Pen Bullet
facts: Pocket size when capped, full size when posted
products.summary: Fisher's pressurized cartridge is made to write upside down and in the cold. Capped, it is about 3.75 inches long; with the cap posted, it is a full-size pen. It looks more expensive than it is.

products.name: Leatherman Micra
facts: Keychain tool built around spring-action scissors
products.summary: Leatherman's keychain tool. Instead of pliers it has proper spring-loaded scissors, which get used far more often for tags, tape and loose threads.

products.name: SENCUT Sachse
facts: Button lock on ceramic ball bearings
products.summary: A full-size folder for camping, yard work and lots of cardboard. It runs smooth on bearings and stays under $50.

products.name: Leatherman Skeletool CX
products.summary: A full-size Leatherman that disappears in a pocket. If the person on your list already has a cheap multitool, this is the one that replaces it for good.

products.name: Leatherman Wave+
products.summary: The multitool that ends up being handed down. It is the classic big gift for a dad, a new homeowner or anyone who fixes things. Eighteen tools, and the ones people use most open from outside without unfolding the handles.

products.name: Opinel No.08 Stainless
products.summary: The French classic: a light wooden-handled folder that has been in pockets for over a century. The stainless blade shrugs off food and damp weather, and a twist of the ring locks it open.

products.name: SENCUT Mims
products.summary: A full-size folder with a grippy G10 handle and a stainless blade, for camping, yard work and a lot of cardboard.

products.name: Gerber Paraframe I
products.summary: A skeletonized steel frame keeps it light and simple. The serrated part of the blade chews through rope, cord and packing straps.

products.name: SENCUT ArcBlast
facts: Button lock, opens by flipper or thumb stud
products.summary: A just-under-3 inch folder with a metal handle that feels solid without weighing down a pocket. The button lock makes it easy to close one handed.

products.name: Spyderco Tenacious G-10
products.summary: Spyderco's long-running budget folder. The thumb hole opens it easily with either hand, and it is a common first step up from a cheap knife.

products.name: Buck 110 Folding Hunter LT
facts: Lockback, comes with a nylon sheath
products.summary: Buck's famous 110 shape in a light handle, so it carries in a pocket or on a belt without the brass weight. A traditional pick for someone who doesn't want anything tactical.

products.name: SENCUT Squiggy
facts: G10 handle with room for big hands
Button lock, flipper and thumb hole
products.summary: The big one of the bunch. Pick it if you have large hands or want the most blade you can get for the money.

products.name: SENCUT Serene
facts: Button lock, flipper or thumb stud
products.summary: A bigger sibling to the ArcBlast, with the same easy one-handed button lock and a longer D2 blade for outdoor work.

products.name: Kershaw Leek
products.summary: A slim, dressy folder that disappears in a pocket and flicks open with assisted opening. A gift that looks more expensive than it is.

products.name: Sofirn SE1
facts: Rechargeable, with UV and RGB modes
products.summary: A coin-sized light for the key ring, with extra UV and colored modes. Cheap enough to buy a few as stocking stuffers.

products.name: Olight iUltra
products.summary: Olight's newer mini keychain light. A tidy step up for someone who already likes the idea of a light on their keys.

products.name: Nitecore TIP3
products.summary: A flat keychain light that also clips to a pocket, with a choice of warm, neutral or cool white.

products.name: Nitecore TINI 3
products.summary: A tiny keychain light with a lot of output for its size, and a choice of light color for reading or finding things in the dark.

products.name: Nitecore THUMB
facts: 85 lumens white, plus a red side light
USB rechargeable, clips to keys or a cap
products.summary: A tiny clip-on light whose head tilts, so it points where you need it while hanging off your keys, a bag strap or a cap brim.

products.name: Olight Oclip Pro
facts: Clips to a pocket, strap or collar
products.summary: A light that clips on instead of riding in a pocket, so both hands stay free for dog walks, runs and car trouble.

products.name: Nitecore EDC09
products.summary: A pocket light with a head that swivels and a magnetic tail, so it can stand on a car hood or point into an engine bay while you work.

products.name: Nitecore EDC29
products.summary: A flat, pocketable light with huge maximum output. It's the big-gift light for someone who already owns a keychain one.

products.name: Streamlight ProTac HL
products.summary: A classic tube light with a tail switch you can work with gloves on. It runs on common lithium batteries, so it keeps working in the cold and in a glovebox for years.

products.name: Leatherman Rev
products.summary: Leatherman's entry-level pocket tool. It has real pliers and drivers at a price that makes it an easy first Leatherman.

products.name: Leatherman Wingman
products.summary: The value pick in Leatherman's full-size lineup. The spring-loaded pliers and scissors open on their own, which people notice the first time they use them.

products.name: Leatherman Rebar
products.summary: A workhorse tool with replaceable wire cutters and a saw, for people who fix things more than they open packages.

products.name: Leatherman Signal
products.summary: Leatherman's outdoor multitool, made for camping and hiking kits rather than the junk drawer.

products.name: Leatherman Surge
products.summary: The big, heavy-duty Leatherman for work trucks, garages and the person who uses their tool every single day.

products.name: Timex Expedition Scout 40mm
products.summary: A plain field watch with hands, a date and a backlight. Easy to read at a glance and casual enough for every day.

products.name: Casio G-Shock DW5600UE
products.summary: The classic square G-Shock. It is built to take knocks, so it's the watch for people who work with their hands and don't want to baby a watch.

products.name: Casio G-Shock GW-M5610U
products.summary: The square G-Shock with solar charging and radio time sync, so it charges from light and sets its own time. The set-and-forget splurge watch.

products.name: Parker Jotter Stainless
products.summary: A slim all-steel click pen that has been around for decades. It costs little, looks smart and takes refills that are easy to find.

products.name: Moleskine Classic Pocket Notebook
products.summary: The pocket notebook most people picture: a hard cover, an elastic band and enough pages to last months.
